children: The long-term Japanese government bond yield hits a 30-year high, driven by inflation concerns and prospects of the Bank of Japan's faster rate increases. Energy costs are rising with no clear end in sight for the Middle East conflict. The BOJ is expected to raise its policy rate later this week to mitigate risks of higher inflation. Investors are focusing on developments in the Middle East as Saudi Arabia races to repair a critical oil pipeline shut by drone attacks last week. The 10-year JGB yield rises 4.5 basis points to 3.030%, its highest level since September 1996. (kosaku.narioka@wsj.com; @kosakunarioka)
